rules.conflictOrdinance: Miami-Dade County Code Sec. 2-11.1 (Conflict of Interest and Code of Ethics Ordinance) applies to municipal officials in the County, including Miami Beach; the City's 2025 candidate handbook requires an affidavit of compliance with Sec. 2-11.1(bb). https://library.municode.com/fl/miami_-_dade_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIIICOOR_CH2AD_ARTIINGE_S2-11.1COINCOET . City of Miami Beach Code ch. 2, art. VII (Standards of Conduct) via https://library.municode.com/fl/miami_beach/codes/code_of_ordinances (specific section URL not captured; municode blocked the fetcher). City clerk ethics and disclosure forms: https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/city-hall/city-clerk/forms/
rules.abstentionRule: F.S. 112.3143(3): a municipal officer may not vote on a measure inuring to the special private gain or loss of the officer, a principal, a relative or a business associate; must state the interest before the vote and file Form 8B within 15 days with the City Clerk for inclusion in the minutes. https://www.leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0112/Sections/0112.3143.html
rules.ethicsBody: Miami-Dade Commission on Ethics and Public Trust (jurisdiction over municipal officials under County Code Sec. 2-1066 et seq.): https://ethics.miamidade.gov/ ; Florida Commission on Ethics: https://ethics.state.fl.us/ ; City of Miami Beach Office of the Inspector General: https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/inspectorgeneral/

notes: Form type for 2025: Form 1. SB 774 (Ch. 2023-49) would have moved municipal mayors and governing-body members to Form 6 from the 2023 reporting year, but the U.S. District Court (S.D. Fla.) in Loper v. Lukis, No. 1:24-cv-20604, entered a preliminary injunction on 2024-06-10 barring enforcement against all elected municipal governing-body members and mayors, who reverted to Form 1; summary judgment was fully briefed by 2024-10-11 with no final judgment as of the Commission's 2024-11-19 litigation memo (https://www.ethics.state.fl.us/Documents/Ethics/MeetingAgendas/Nov24Materials/Litigation.pdf). The Miami Beach 2025 candidate handbook lists Form 1 as the qualifying disclosure (https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/2025-HANDBOOK-FINAL-VERSION-REG-FINAL-FOR-PUBLICATION-1.pdf-1-1.pdf, p. 10). The specific form each commissioner filed for 2025 was not verified because the EFDMS grid did not load. Florida EFDMS public search (https://disclosure.floridaethics.gov/PublicSearch/Filings) renders its results grid client-side; the fetcher sees only 'No records to display' on the results page (/PublicSearch/FilingsResults?FirstName=..&LastName=..&FormYear=..) and the per-filer history page (/PublicSearch/FilingHistory/<PID>). Direct filing PDFs exist at /api/Report/RenderPdf/<id>/False but the id is only exposed by the search grid. No form captured; needs a browser session. Abstentions: Miami Beach commission agendas and minutes after 2024-06-26 are on PrimeGov (https://portal-miamibeachfl.primegov.com/), which loads its meeting list client-side and was empty to the fetcher; the city's WordPress PDF uploads (after-action reports, Official Actions) are robots-blocked. No Form 8B or abstention for a current commissioner, 2025 to 2026, could be read.  Ethics: Miami-Dade COE minutes 2025-09 through 2026-04 and the 2024-11-13 summary name no current Miami Beach commissioner or the Mayor (INQ 25-115, 2025-12-10 minutes, concerned a person seeking a Commission seat, not an officeholder). Florida COE 2026 press releases name none.
